title: Sodom and Gomorrah
lead: Two cities near the Dead Sea destroyed by fire in Genesis 19. Ever after, the Bible uses them as the standard picture of sudden, total judgment, and names many sins of Sodom.

sections.b: Lot settled near Sodom, whose people were "very wicked" (Genesis 13:12–13). Abraham bargained with God for the city if ten righteous people could be found (Genesis 18:16–33). Two angels came to Lot; the men of the city surrounded the house and demanded to "know" them; the angels led Lot's family out, and fire and sulfur fell (Genesis 19).

The prophets use Sodom for total ruin (Deuteronomy 29:23; Isaiah 1:9–10; Jeremiah 49:18; Amos 4:11) and name its sins: injustice (Isaiah 1:10–17), adultery and lies (Jeremiah 23:14), and "pride, excess of food and careless ease," not helping the poor, and "they were haughty and did an abomination before me" (Ezekiel 16:49–50). Readers differ on whether that "abomination" includes the sexual sin of Genesis 19. Jesus says a town that rejects his messengers will fare worse than Sodom (Matthew 10:15; Luke 10:12), and uses Sodom for the suddenness of judgment (Luke 17:28–32).
